job.title: Inspector Grade III – Chemical Enforcement, COMAH, Chemical Production and Storage & The Transport of Dangerous Goods by Road (ADR)
job.description:
HSA Candidate Booklet Grade III Chemical Enforcement COMAH, Chemical Production and Storage & The Transport of Dangerous Goods by Road (ADR).pdf


HSA Grade III Chemical Enforcement COMAH, Chemical Production and Storage & The Transport (ADR) - Application Form.docx


The Health and Safety Authority (HSA) are recruiting for Inspectors at Grade III level. The roles involve monitoring and enforcing compliance with the Chemicals Acts, the European Communities Act and the relevant legislation associated with the Control of Major Accident Hazards (COMAH) and the transport of dangerous goods by road (ADR) all based in our Chemicals and Industrial Products Division to help us do what we do best, making a difference to workers across Ireland by keeping them safe and protected.


Key Responsibilities:

The following non-exhaustive list of tasks are those that a Grade III Inspector could be assigned. Please note that the final set of tasks will reflect the role the person is offered: 


  • Carry out inspections in the areas of control of major accident hazards, chemical production and storage, or transport of dangerous goods by road up to and including enforcement action.
  • Assess and prepare technical responses on submissions (for example under the COMAH area safety reports, significant modification assessment reports and planning advice requests.)
  • Investigation and follow up of accidents and incidents, preparation of reports of investigation including for legal proceedings.
  • Liaise with local authorities, fire authorities, the Gardaí and HSE on technical advice and external emergency planning under the 2015 COMAH Regulations.
  • Build a relevant technical network with other relevant regulators.
  • Develop and maintain technical expertise in process safety or transport of dangerous goods.
  • Contribute to development of policies and procedures.
  • Support awareness raising activities, engage with relevant stakeholders and represent the Authority at meetings with stakeholders, as required.
  • Research technical queries to support the activities of the Authority’s Helpdesk and Contact Centre.
  • Contribute to Competent Authority functions at national and EU level.
  • Undertakes other such duties as may be assigned in accordance with the operational needs of the Authority.


This post requires flexibility and accordingly, an Inspector Grade III must be prepared to undertake other work and responsibilities as may be assigned from time to time. The role may involve some EU travel.


Essential Criteria:

In addition to demonstrating that you possess the required competencies, the ideal candidate must be able to demonstrate:


  • Primary degree (NFQ level 8 or equivalent) in engineering or science or other appropriate qualification relevant to the role.
  • Minimum of two years relevant experience in regulatory, industry setting.
  • Possession of a full driving licence (Category B).


Desirable Requirements:

In addition to the above essential requirements, it would be a decided advantage for candidates to have one or more of the following:


  •  A recognised qualification in the area of Process Safety (COMAH Inspector).
  • Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser (DGSA) certification (ADR Inspector).
  • A recognised qualification in the area of Health and Safety.
  • Experience in preparing or reviewing technical reports.
  • Familiarity with the Control of Major Accident Hazard Regulations, or ADR.


Further details can be found in the Candidate Booklet (linked below).

The Health and Safety Authority (HSA) is recruiting a Project Manager on a three-year fixed-term contract to join its Corporate Services Division. This is an exciting opportunity to play a central role in supporting the delivery of strategic projects and transformation initiatives across the Authority.


Working closely with senior management, business leads and external partners, the successful candidate will help translate strategic priorities into successful outcomes through effective planning, governance and delivery. The role requires a strong focus on project management, stakeholder engagement and organisational change, with responsibility for establishing effective project governance arrangements, supporting informed decision-making, managing risks and dependencies, and ensuring projects are delivered successfully and achieve their intended benefits.


This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to initiatives that will strengthen the Authority's future capability, including programmes involving digital transformation, organisational development, workplace change, service improvement and other strategic priorities.


Key Responsibilities:

The following above list is not exhaustive and may be amended to meet the changing needs of the Authority.


  • Lead and support the delivery of significant organisational projects and transformation initiatives.
  • Establish and maintain effective project governance, planning, reporting and risk management arrangements.
  • Provide strategic leadership for organisational change initiatives, ensuring that change impacts, stakeholder engagement, communications, governance arrangements, capability development, and benefits realisation activities are planned and managed effectively to achieve successful adoption and sustainable outcomes.
  • Support senior decision-making through the provision of high-quality project information, analysis and reporting.
  • Ensure a strong focus on outcomes, benefits realisation and continuous improvement.
  • Introduce and embed project management methodology and best practice and contribute to strengthening organisational project delivery capability.


Essential Criteria:

In addition to demonstrating that you possess the required competencies, the ideal candidate must be able to demonstrate:


  • Hold a minimum NFQ Level 8 qualification (or equivalent) in a relevant discipline.
  • Have a minimum of five years’ relevant experience leading and delivering complex projects or programmes involving multiple stakeholders and significant organisational impact.
  • Have a proven track record of establishing effective project governance arrangements, including planning, reporting, risk management and stakeholder engagement.
  • Demonstrate strong leadership, communication and influencing skills, with the ability to build effective relationships.
  • Have experience driving organisational change and supporting the successful implementation of new systems, processes or ways of working.
  • Demonstrate the competencies required for the role as set out in Appendix 4.


Desirable Requirements:

In addition to the above essential requirements, it would be a decided advantage for candidates to have one or more of the following:


  •  A recognised qualification or certification in project management (e.g. PRINCE2, PMP, MSP, Agile or equivalent).

job.title: Assistant Principal: Talent and Capability
job.description:
Booklet Assistant Principal Talent and Capability.pdf


HSA Assistant Principal Talent and Capability - Application Form Sept 2026.docx


The Assistant Principal – Talent and Capability is an important management role within the wider People and Organisational Development Team.

The postholder will lead the Learning and Development function, support talent and capability initiatives, and work closely with managers across the Authority to help build the skills, confidence and capacity needed to deliver the HSA’s strategic objectives. This role will suit a practical, collaborative and solutions-focused person who can think on their feet, bring fresh ideas and support a positive culture of continuous improvement, professional development and high performance.

This is an opportunity for a proactive and curious Learning and Development professional to make a visible contribution to how the Authority builds 

capability, supports managers and develops its people. The successful candidate will bring sound judgement, practical problem-solving skills and the confidence to contribute constructive ideas in a busy public sector environment.


Roles and responsibilities


  • Develop, implement and review practical talent, learning and capability strategies, policies and workplans that support the Authority’s strategic objectives, workforce needs and wider People and Organisational Development priorities.
  • Lead the identification of organisational, team and individual learning and capability needs, using skills gap analysis, engagement with managers, workforce planning priorities and sound judgement to identify where learning interventions can have the greatest impact.
  • Translate identified learning needs into practical Learning and Development plans, programmes and interventions that support current and future business requirements.
  • Manage the day-to-day delivery and continuous improvement of the Authority’s Learning and Development function, including the annual programme of learning activities, leadership development initiatives, professional development supports and related evaluation processes.
  • Oversee the implementation of employee development, leadership and talent initiatives, ensuring that programmes are well planned, appropriately procured, effectively delivered and evaluated for impact against agreed objectives.
  • Manage the Authority’s PMDS process from a learning, development and performance-support perspective, including coordinating timelines, monitoring returns, following up with managers and identifying development themes that can inform future learning priorities.
  • Provide practical, solutions-focused advice and support to people managers on learning, development, performance management and related people matters, working collaboratively with colleagues across the People and Organisational Development Team to respond to business needs.
  • Contribute to the development of the People and Organisational Development Team as a trusted, responsive and credible business partner to the organisation, supporting consistent, professional and people-centred service delivery to managers and staff.
  • Work with senior managers and colleagues to support organisational culture, engagement, equality, diversity and inclusion priorities, including the development and delivery of relevant training, awareness initiatives and practical supports that encourage positive behaviours across the Authority.
  • Oversee the annual Learning and Development budget, ensuring that expenditure is planned, monitored and aligned with organisational priorities, public sector governance requirements and value-for-money principles.
  • Manage the Authority’s Learning and Development Committee, including planning meetings, preparing agendas and papers, recording decisions and actions, and following up with relevant managers to support delivery.
  • Lead the procurement, development and implementation of a Learning Management System, working with relevant stakeholders to deliver a user-friendly platform that supports effective learning administration, reporting, evaluation and staff experience.
  • Participate in relevant cross-organisational groups, including the Authority’s Wellbeing Committee, and coordinate agreed learning, wellbeing or engagement activities that support staff development, participation and organisational priorities.
  • Manage assigned projects and programmes within the annual People and Organisational Development work programme, bringing structure, energy and follow-through to ensure that activities are delivered on time, to the required standard and in support of the HSA Strategy.
  • Carry out other appropriate duties within the remit of the People and Organisational Development Unit as assigned by management


Essential Criteria:

The ideal candidate must be able to demonstrate:


  • A relevant Level 8 qualification or higher in human resources, organisational development, learning and development, talent management, business, management, or another discipline relevant to the role.
  • A minimum of five years’ relevant experience in learning and development, organisational development, human resources, talent management, performance development or a related people-focused function.
  • The competencies required for the role, as set out in Appendix 4, including the ability to work collaboratively, exercise sound judgement, manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes.


Desirable Requirements:

In addition to the above essential requirements, it would be a decided advantage for candidates to have:


  • A further qualification or professional development in training, learning and development, organisational development, human resources management or a related discipline.
  • Membership of CIPD or eligibility for membership.
  • Experience in developing, implementing or supporting capability, learning or talent development strategies, programmes or initiatives.
  • Previous public sector experience, or experience working within a governed, regulated or policy-led environment, together with an understanding of governance requirements and central policies applicable to public sector bodies.

HSA Grade III - Market Surveillance of Industrial Products - Appliction Form.docx


The Health and Safety Authority (HSA) are recruiting a highly motivated and experienced professional to join our Industrial Products team.

The role is under our regulatory mandate for market surveillance of industrial products encompassing our activities under product safety legislation including machinery, personal protective equipment, gas appliances, pressure equipment, transportable pressure equipment, ATEX, Lifts and lifting equipment. The role involves the market surveillance of products and enforcement of compliance with the European Communities Acts, the Safety Health and Welfare at Work Act and the relevant legislation governing industrial products.


The role also consists of participation in and support of EU wide enforcement market surveillance campaigns. The Inspector will be working as part of a dynamic team and contributing to the performance of Competent Authority functions under EU and national legislation. This role may also require

some EU travel.


Key Responsibilities:

The following non-exhaustive list of tasks are those that a Grade III Inspector could be assigned. Please note that the final set of tasks will reflect the role the person is offered: 


  • Contributing to the Authorities Competent Authority inspection and market surveillance related functions.
  • Carry out inspections, audits and market surveillance of products up to and including enforcement action.
  • Conduct assessments of products, including online (documentary checks, screening analysis/testing).
  • Input and participate into national and EU coordinated product enforcement projects.
  • Monitor and follow up of Safety Gate alerts.
  • Undertaking risk assessments for high hazard “serious risk” industrial products.
  • Ensuring the accurate and timely entering of information and data onto the relevant information technology platforms.
  • Developing, maintaining and providing technical expertise related to industrial products regulated by the Authority.
  • Participation in European meetings and working groups.
  • Supporting awareness raising activities, engaging with relevant stakeholders and representing the Authority at meetings with stakeholders, as required.
  • Contributing to the development of guidance, policy and procedures.
  • Researching technical queries to support the activities of the Authority’s contact centre.


This post requires flexibility and accordingly, in addition to the above responsibilities, an Inspector Grade III must be prepared to undertake other work and responsibilities in accordance with the operational needs of the Authority.


Essential Criteria:

In addition to demonstrating that you possess the required competencies, the ideal candidate must be able to demonstrate:


  • Primary degree (NFQ level 8 or equivalent) in engineering, science or other appropriate qualification relevant to the role.
  • Minimum of two years relevant experience in a regulatory, industry or a post graduate setting.
  • Possession of a full driving licence (Category B).


Desirable Requirements:

In addition to the above essential requirements, it would be a decided advantage for candidates to have one or more of the following:

HSA Inspector Grade II Chemical Regulatory Policy - Application Form Sept 2026.docx



The Health and Safety Authority (HSA) is recruiting Grade II Inspectors to its chemical policy team.


The roles involve supporting the development and implementation of chemicals policy and legislation at national and EU level. The roles involve

evaluating the need for EU wide measures to regulate chemicals, reviewing legislative proposals, coordinating policy positions, engaging with stakeholders, and contributing to strategic regulatory initiatives. The roles will also involve actioning relevant activities under the One Substance One Assessment (OSOA) regulatory framework, which aims to improve the consistency, transparency, and efficiency of chemical hazard and risk assessments across EU legislation. The successful candidates will be responsible for evaluating information and preparing opinions and/or briefings supporting effective decision making on the safe management and use of chemicals at an EU level. The roles will require representation of the Authority in national and EU technical and expert working groups and committees.


Key Responsibilities:

Key accountabilities for the roles include, but are not limited to, the following:


  • Deliver on Competent Authority functions for EU Chemicals Regulations (REACH, CLP, OSOA) under the Authority’s remit at national and EU level.
  • Monitoring and evaluating developments in EU chemicals legislation and policy.
  • Analysing legislative proposals and their potential impacts on actors in the supply chain.
  • Drafting policy papers, briefing documents and position statements.
  • Participate in EU fora and working groups as required, including attendance at EU meetings
  • Review and draft observations on scientific opinions and/or regulatory proposals circulated by ECHA and/or other Member States.
  • Advising and briefing internal stakeholders and Departmental officials.
  • Engage with relevant stakeholders and represent the Authority at meetings with stakeholders and representative bodies as well as in public forums,as required.
  • Maintain good communications with stakeholders e.g. by attending meetings, giving presentations, answering Chemical Helpdesk queries etc.
  • Support development and delivery of the Authority’s Strategic objectives and annual Programme of Work.
  • Lead on development of relevant policies and/or technical innovation, and legislative areas.
  • Develop, maintain and contribute to the development of technical expertise on changing scientific developments.
  • May be required to manage a team of direct reports, creating a positive working environment and supporting their professional and personal development and their continuous improvement.
  • Undertake such other duties as may be assigned in accordance with the operational needs of the Authority.


Please note that the final set of tasks will be assigned on take up of the roles.


Essential Criteria:

The following requirements are essential:


  • Primary degree (NFQ level 8 or equivalent) in a Science-related discipline (e.g. Environmental, Toxicology, Chemistry, Regulatory Science) or other appropriate relevant discipline to the roles.
  • Minimum of three years relevant work experience, with significant experience in chemicals regulation, policy development, regulatory affairs or a related field in a regulatory or industry setting.
  • Good knowledge and understanding of relevant EU/Irish legislation.
  • Possession of a full driving licence (Category B).
  • Demonstrate possession of the required competencies for the roles.


Desirable Requirements:

In addition to the above essential requirements, it would be a decided advantage for candidates to have one or more of the following:


  • Post graduate qualification in science/ chemicals-related regulatory field.
  • Experience in the area of risk management at EU level.
  • Previous experience of participation at national or European committees or working groups.
  • Experience in the management of projects and staff.


Further details can be found in the Candidate Booklet (linked below).

job.title: Manager - Digital, AI and Conversion
job.description:
Key Details:

 

Location: Dublin, Sligo, Galway or Cork

 

Contract: Full-time, permanent

 

Salary: €69,149 – €109,980 (starting at the first point of the scale)

 

Closing date: Thursday 14 October 2026 at 3pm


Failte Ireland_Manager - Digital, AI and Conversion _Application Form.docx


Reporting to the Head of Digital, AI and Conversion, the Manager will lead programmes that help tourism businesses grow by improving their digital capability, increasing online sales and converting more customer interest into bookings, visits and revenue.

 

The role will focus on supporting small and medium-sized tourism businesses across Ireland. It will work with businesses, industry partners and stakeholders to understand business needs and deliver practical supports that help businesses attract customers, improve online presence, convert interest into bookings and build long-term capability.

 

A key part of the role will be helping businesses make better use of digital tools, data and AI in practical and responsible ways. This means identifying where technology can help businesses solve real problems, improve how they work, make better decisions, reach more customers and increase conversion. The successful candidate does not need to be a technical specialist but should be confident in understanding business needs and translating digital, data and AI opportunities into clear supports that can help businesses grow online. 

 

Key Responsibilities:

 

Tourism Business Support and Development

 

·     Manage the design and delivery of programmes that help tourism businesses improve customer engagement, online sales, booking conversion, marketing, productivity and overall business capability.

·     Work directly with tourism businesses to understand their needs and identify practical supports that can make a real difference.

·     Ensure programmes are relevant, accessible and useful for small and medium-sized businesses.

·     Help businesses strengthen their ability to attract customers, improve sales, convert interest into action and build long-term resilience.

·     Use feedback from businesses and industry partners to improve existing supports and shape future programme activity.

 

Digital, AI and Conversion Improvement 

 

·     Support tourism businesses to make better use of digital tools, data and AI where these can improve business performance, increase online sales and support stronger conversion.

·     Manage the development of practical guidance, resources and programmes that help businesses improve their online presence, reach the right customers, increase direct sales and convert more interest into bookings.

·     Use data, customer insights and business feedback to identify where businesses are losing sales online and shape practical supports to address these gaps.

·     Keep informed about relevant digital and AI trends and consider how they can help tourism businesses improve customer engagement, sales and conversion.

·     Translate digital and AI opportunities into clear, practical advice that helps non-technical audiences take action and improve commercial results.

 

Programme and Project Management

 

·     Manage programmes from planning through to delivery, review and reporting.

·     Set clear objectives, timelines, budgets and measures of success for each programme, including measures linked to online sales, customer engagement and conversion where relevant.

·     Manage delivery partners, suppliers and external service providers to ensure high-quality delivery.

·     Monitor progress, identify risks and take action to keep programmes on track.

·     Evaluate programme results using evidence, including business feedback, sales outcomes and conversion-related measures where available, to improve future activity

 

Industry and Stakeholder Relationships

 

·     Build strong relationships with tourism businesses, industry bodies, government departments, state agencies and other partners.

·     Act as a trusted contact for stakeholders involved in business support and tourism development.

·     Work with partners to avoid duplication and ensure businesses can access the right support at the right time.

·     Encourage collaboration across the tourism and enterprise support system.

·     Represent the needs of tourism businesses in internal planning and programme development.

 

Cross-Organisational Collaboration 

 

·     Work closely with teams across Fáilte Ireland to ensure coordinated programme planning, delivery and performance measurement.

·     Collaborate with internal teams across Fáilte Ireland to ensure coordinated operationalisation and measurement of grant-funded digitalisation schemes. 

·     Work closely with internal teams to ensure support programmes are aligned with wider priorities for digital adoption, online sales growth, conversion and business resilience.

·     Ensure all activity contributes to wider organisational priorities including regional development, sustainability, accessibility, inclusion and business resilience.

 

 

Team Management and Governance 

 

·     Manage, coach and support assigned team members to deliver agreed objectives.

·     Create a collaborative, practical and business-focused approach within the team.

·     Manage programme budgets, procurement processes and delivery contracts in line with Fáilte Ireland policies and public sector requirements.

·     Monitor programme performance through effective measurement frameworks, provide clear progress updates, performance reports and risk updates to the Head of Digital, AI and Conversion.

·     Ensure all projects comply with public spending guidelines, public financial procedures and State Aid requirements, maintaining appropriate governance and risk documentation.

·     Ensure strong programme governance, compliance and financial management across all assigned programmes and activities 

·     Oversee the effective closure and transition of existing digitalisation programmes and associated supplier contracts, ensuring all reporting, audit, financial and contractual obligations are fulfilled. Support the ongoing collection and analysis of programme performance data to demonstrate impact and support future investment decisions.

 

Corporate Responsibility

job.title: Head of Data Economics
job.description:
Key Details:

Location: Dublin, Limerick or Cork

Contract: Full-time, permanent

Salary: €105,041 – €133,335 (starting at the first point of the scale)

Closing date: Thursday 15 October 2026 at 3pm

Reports to: Director of Data, Insights and Economics


Download Application Form: Failte Ireland_Head of Data Economics_Application Form.docx


Fáilte Ireland's Corporate Strategy 2026–2029 places data and evidence at the core of how the organisation plans, invests in and grows Irish tourism. To deliver this ambition, Fáilte Ireland has established a new Directorate - Data, Insights and Economic Services - bringing together six divisions responsible for data, insight and economic analysis across the organisation. Five of these divisions continue existing functions under revised remits; Data Economics is an entirely new division, created to lead the organisation's data strategy, standards and capability. 

 

This is a significant and rare opportunity: the successful candidate will establish Data Economics from the ground up, shaping its team, standards and culture, and defining how Fáilte Ireland's data underpins tourism policy, investment and enterprise decisions for years to come.


Role Purpose 

The Head of Data Economics is a senior leadership role, responsible for setting the strategic direction, standards and capability that put data at the centre of decision-making across Fáilte Ireland. The role leads the development and implementation of Fáilte Ireland's data strategy, establishing and leading the organisation's Tourism Data Office — the central hub that owns the standards, architecture, systems and tools that turn the organisation's data into a trusted foundation for tourism insight, policy and investment decisions. 

 

The directorates five other divisions generate deep domain data and analysis across their own areas of expertise. The Head of Data Economics owns the data strategy, standards and data integrity that connect this into a single, coherent evidence base, ensuring every division and stakeholder across the organisation can find, trust and act on it. 

 

Enabling every part of the organisation to access, interpret and act on evidence with confidence is a shared responsibility across the Directorate's leadership team; the Head of Data Economics leads this by providing the underlying data, standards and tools that make it possible for every division. 

Delivering this strategy draws on a range of analytical, technical and digital capability, including the application of AI to drive efficiency, insource analytical work that would otherwise be contracted externally, and build modern, self-service data tools. AI is one of several capabilities this role applies in service of the data strategy: the role's primary focus is data leadership across the organisation. 

 

In time the team will lead the establishment of a Tourism Futures Lab — Ireland's tourism equivalent of Bord Bia's Thinking House. Rather than a research project that sits on a shelf, it will be a living hub giving destinations, clients and policymakers direct access to global trends, foresight and scenario modelling that no single organisation could build or afford alone. Delivered in partnership with academia, EU initiatives and other research bodies, the Lab will let the whole tourism system see further ahead, test what's coming, and attract the private investment needed to act on it. 

 

Key Responsibilities:

 

Tourism Data Office (TDO) 

  • Establish and lead a permanent Tourism Data Office within Fáilte Ireland as the organisation's central data hub, bringing tourism data together across Fáilte Ireland and partner organisations. 
  • Own the standards for data quality, governance, ethics and release calendars that the TDO runs on, holding every division to a single, trusted way of working with data. 
  • Build shared data capability across the tourism ecosystem, and develop clear, plain-English “explain the insight” narratives that make data and analysis usable by policymakers, destination teams, SMEs and non-specialist colleagues. 

 

Data Strategy & Standards Leadership 

  • Lead the development and implementation of Fáilte Ireland's data strategy, setting the direction for how data is captured, governed, connected and used across the organisation. 
  • Own data integrity across the organisation — the definitive authority on the data standards and quality that every division works to. 
  • Lead the development and implementation of data standards and processes that give every division a common, trusted way of working with data. 
  • Partner closely with the other five divisions and other data sources in the organisation — who own the deep domain data and analysis in their areas — so the strategy, standards and tools this role leads are built around what they actually need to turn their own data into decisions. 

 

Data Architecture & Centralisation 

  • Design and lead the build of a secure, scalable core tourism data architecture that centralises data from across Fáilte Ireland and partner organisations into a single, shareable evidence base. 
  • Apply the organisation's data standards and quality controls consistently across the architecture, reducing duplication and enabling a single shared evidence base for national, regional and enterprise-level decisions. 
  • Ensure sensitive data is protected while enabling broad, role-appropriate access — the aim is more people across the organisation using the data, not fewer. 

 

Data Tools to Deliver the Strategy 

  • Develop the data tools — dashboards, calculators, AI-assisted query tools — that deliver the data strategy in practice for both internal teams and external industry/SME stakeholders. 
  • Build self-service products that put data and insight directly into stakeholders' hands, reducing reliance on bespoke, one-off analytical requests. 
  • Continuously identify where recurring demand for data or analysis signals the need for a new self-service tool. 

 

Economic Impact, Modelling & Forecasting 

  • Maintain and refresh tourism economic impact measurement tools and sharing mechanisms. 
  • Develop analytical tools that showcase tourism's economic contribution, test policy and investment choices, and provide early warning signals on future performance. 
  • Build economic modelling and forecasting frameworks that help the organisation understand how tourism value flows through the economy and what is likely to happen next. 

 

Applying AI to Strengthen Delivery 

  • Apply AI to drive efficiency in day-to-day data management and analysis — data cleaning, reconciliation, reporting and routine modelling - and to insource analytical work currently contracted externally, delivering measurable budget savings. 
  • Lead Fáilte Ireland's AI strategy and adoption roadmap as it relates to data and analysis, including chairing the internal AI Steering Group, so the organisation applies AI consistently and responsibly in support of the data strategy. 

 

Tourism Futures Lab 

  • Develop and lead a Tourism Futures Lab in partnership with academia, EU initiatives and other research bodies. 
  • Advance applied foresight, scenario modelling and long-term tourism system analysis. 
  • Support advanced tourism investment modelling to attract and inform private investment. 
  • Scan global trends and structural shifts affecting tourism demand, supply, investment and competitiveness. 

 

Resource Management 

  • Establish, inspire, lead and develop the Data Economics team to deliver agreed objectives, fostering high performance, collaboration and accountability through effective coaching, mentoring and performance reviews in line with Fáilte Ireland policy. 

 

Governance & Reporting 

  • Ensure strong governance across all Data Economics activity, complying with Fáilte Ireland policies on planning, procurement, budgets and reporting, with tight control of team expenditure within agreed budgets. 
  • Act as an active member of the Leadership Team, providing timely status updates, insights and risk escalation to the Director and Executive colleagues, and systematically reviewing progress against plans and KPIs. 
  • Provide strategic leadership and oversight across the Division, ensuring effective project and risk management, robust financial governance, compliance with State Aid requirements, and adherence to public spending obligations and public financial procedures. 

 

Skills and Competencies Required 

 

  • A strong track record of leading the development and implementation of organisation-wide data strategy, including data governance and responsibility for setting the direction and requirements for data architecture. 
  • Demonstrable experience of turning complex data and evidence into strategic insight and recommendations, with clear examples of their impact on organisational, policy or investment decisions. 
  • Demonstrable experience of leading, commissioning or quality-assuring economic modelling, forecasting and applied economic analysis to inform strategic decision-making. 
  • Strong knowledge of research design and advanced quantitative and qualitative methods, with experience of setting analytical direction and assuring the quality and relevance of research and analysis. 
  • Demonstrable experience of establishing and maintaining organisational standards for data governance, ethics, integrity and quality assurance. 
  • The ability to translate complex analysis into clear, plain-English implications and recommendations for non-specialist stakeholders, and to lead the development and implementation of tools that make insight accessible and actionable. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrable experience of advising and influencing Executive, policy and industry stakeholders. 
  • Proven senior people-leadership experience, with the ability to establish, lead and develop a new multidisciplinary team and organisational function. 
  • A practical understanding of AI and automation, with demonstrable experience of leading their responsible organisational adoption to strengthen data management, analysis and efficiency. 
  • Strong attention to detail and analytical rigour. 

 

Relevant Fáilte Ireland Competencies 

﻿

  • Strategic Thinking 
  • Decision Making 
  • Inspire and Engage 
  • Embracing Innovation 

 

Annual Leave & Blended Working

 

Annual Leave: This role offers 29 days of annual leave per annum.

 

Blended Working

We do not ask for addresses as part of the application process, however it is the responsibility of the candidate to acknowledge the base location of the role. The successful candidate must regularly work from and attend the base office location of the role.

Please note: Remote working from outside the State is not permitted other than in exceptional circumstances. As this role is within the Irish public service, the post-holder must carry out a minimum of 80% of their working time within the State (Republic of Ireland). Candidates who reside in Northern Ireland must be able to meet this requirement.


Selection Process

Shortlisting will be based on applications and the selection process may involve two competency based interviews. A panel of successful candidates may be formed following the selection process.


Interview Attendance Requirement

Candidates must be available to attend an in-person interview at the location and date specified by Fáilte Ireland. Please note that the location of the interview may vary from the base location of the role.

About IN2 

Formed in 2002, IN2 is a progressive engineering consultancy operating across Ireland, the UK, and Europe, dedicated to creating better spaces for people. With over 100 experts across six locations, our team of engineers, technicians, and consultants collaborate closely with clients and partners to deliver innovative, sustainable, and energy-efficient building solutions across a wide range of sectors—from concept and design through to handover and beyond. 

For over 20 years, we have maintained a people-centric culture that encourages growth, innovation, and adaptability. Our award-winning MEP projects, combined with recognition as a ‘Great Place to Work’, reflect our commitment to quality, sustainability, and a supportive, inclusive work environment where individuals can thrive. 

At IN2, joining our team means being part of a collaborative, high-performing, and forward-thinking organisation, where your contribution makes a real impact—and where career opportunities grow alongside our business. 

 

Working Hours  

We operate a 37.5-hour working week designed to support work-life balance. We offer flexible start and finish times between 8am and 6pm, provided that core hours of 10am to 4pm are covered for team collaboration and meetings.  

 

About The Role 

We are seeking an experienced Electrical Engineer to join our growing Athlone team. This is a permanent position offering an excellent package for the right candidate.  You’ll play a key role in project delivery and receive mentorship from senior engineers to support your career development. 


What you will do 

Athlone offers the chance to do career-defining work without long commutes or city pressure. You will be trusted, supported, and encouraged to shape how things are done locally, with full backing from the wider IN2 team.  As a Senior Electrical Engineer at our Athlone Office, you will:   

  • Assist senior engineers with project management, on-site inspections, technical surveys, and design team meetings 
  • Play an active role in project delivery from concept through to completion 
  • Support the management team in client relationships, budgeting, and reporting 
  • Contribute to mentoring junior staff, reviewing design work, and providing guidance 
  • Collaborate with senior engineers for ongoing mentorship and growth 


Your Experience 

To be considered for this role, you should have:  


Essential 

  • Degree in Building Services Engineering or Electrical Engineering 
  • Minimum of 4 years’ experience in electrical design, ideally within a consultancy environment 
  • Passion for career progression and aspiration to achieve Chartered status (if not already obtained) 


Why You’ll Love Being Part of the Team 

At IN2, we’ve traded the stuffy corporate ladder for a flat hierarchy and a culture where your voice actually matters. We’re a diverse, collaborative team that believes the best ideas can come from anyone, anywhere. 

  • Global Impact, Local Feel: You’ll get to work on game-changing projects across different countries, supported by our specialist BIM, Sustainability, and Building Physics teams. 
  • Constant Growth: Through IN2 Talks, cross-office collaboration, and a culture of knowledge sharing, you’re always learning something new. 
  • Your Best Self: We prioritise a genuine work-life balance with flexible hours and support for personal circumstances. We’re big on open communication and ensuring our workplace is a bias-free zone where you can truly be yourself. 


What’s In It For You? 

We’ve put together a package that looks after your wallet, your career, and your wellbeing. 


The Essentials 

  • Competitive Pay & Bonuses: A salary that reflects your worth, plus an annual bonus and pension contributions. 
  • Annual Leave: 22 days of annual leave, scaling up to 27 days as you grow with us (plus all those bank holidays!). 
  • Flexible Hours: Work-life balance isn't just a buzzword here—we offer a 37.5-hour working week with flexible hours (8am–6pm), to suit your lifestyle! 


Career Progression 

  • Personal Roadmap: You’ll have a dedicated Personal Development Plan and mentoring from our senior leaders. 
  • The IN2 Academy: Access to our internal academy, CPD support, and expert assistance in advancing your career,  

 

Health & Wellbeing 

  • Mind & Body: Access to our Employee Assistance Program, annual health checks, and various fitness initiatives. 
  • Commute Greener: Take advantage of our Cycle to Work scheme to keep active on your way to the office. 


Social & Community 

  • Legendary Events: From our famous Christmas party weekend to Employee Appreciation Day and regular staff social events. 
  • Giving Back: Get involved with our team-led charity initiatives. 
  • International Reach: opportunities to work across IN2 offices in London, Dublin, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone, and Madrid 


Eligibility: Due to regulatory requirements, this role is open to candidates with permanent residency or unrestricted right to work in Ireland only. Applications requiring visa sponsorship cannot be considered.

job.title: Senior Electrical Engineer
job.description:
Senior Electrical Engineer

Own the outcome. Not just the design.

Senior Engineers at IN2 lead from the front, responsible for decisions, direction, and delivery across multiple high-value projects.


The Role

As a Senior Electrical Engineer at IN2, you will take ownership of electrical design delivery across major projects, helping shape technical

direction, maintain quality, and build trusted relationships with clients and project teams. This is a hands-on role for someone who can

lead confidently, think strategically, and deliver to a high standard.


What You'll Do

  • Lead electrical design across multiple high-value projects
  • Oversee technical delivery and quality standards
  • Act as a key client contact and build long-term relationships
  • Coordinate with internal teams and external stakeholders
  • Mentor and support junior engineers
  • Contribute to innovation and sustainability strategies



What You'll Bring

  • Degree in Electrical or Building Services Engineering
  • 6+ years' experience in electrical design
  • Strong technical knowledge of building systems and standards
  • Experience leading projects and managing clients
  • Chartered or working towards Chartership desirable
  • Strong leadership and communication skills



What You'll Get 

This isn't built around perks. It's built around how high-performing engineers actually want to work. Real ownership, real progression,

and a culture that trusts you to deliver.


The Essentials

  • Competitive salary, bonus and pension that reflect your impact
  • 22 to 27 days annual leave, plus bank holidays
  • Flexible working across a 37.5 hour week: early start or later start? you decide

Career Progression

  • A clear path forward, with responsibility increasing as you prove it
  • Direct exposure to senior leaders, not layers of hierarchy
  • IN2 Academy, CPD support and chartership guidance
  • Fully paid professional fees

Health and Wellbeing

  • Employee Assistance Programme and annual health checks
  • Wellbeing and fitness initiatives that support you long term
  • Cycle to Work scheme to make the everyday easier

Social and Community

  • Genuinely strong team culture, built through regular events and shared wins
  • Employee-led charity initiatives with real involvement
  • Offices in Dublin, London, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone and Madrid



Why IN2?

Across every role, electrical, mechanical, or BIM, the IN2 difference is the same: you're expected to think, lead, and shape outcomes, not just execute instructions. Here's what sets us apart.

Ownership from Day One

Whether you're an Engineer or a Senior, you'll have real accountability and decision-making authority. No waiting for permission. No layers of sign-off slowing you down.

Progression Based on Ability

Faster progression based on what you deliver, not how long you've been in the seat. A clear pathway from Engineer to Senior, Associate, and beyond.

Innovation Time

Dedicated time to develop new ideas, explore emerging technologies, and contribute to sustainability strategies: built into how we work, not bolted on.

High-Performance, Low-Ego Culture

A team that challenges each other, supports each other, and wins together. No hierarchy for hierarchy's sake. Just talented people doing exceptional work.

Complex, High-Profile Projects

Exposure to design-led, high-impact developments that push the boundaries of what building services engineering can achieve.

Global Reach

Work across offices in Dublin, London, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone, and Madrid- a genuinely international practice with a collaborative, connected culture.


Ready to own the outcome? Join a team that expects more and gives more in return.

job.title: Cyber Underwriter
job.description:
Does it ever feel like you’re underwriting with one hand tied behind your back? Tired of the struggles and inefficiencies associated with legacy systems and processes? Spending too much of your time and energy navigating corporate politics? All leaving your efforts to innovate and deliver underwriting excellence languishing?

At Ledgebrook, we believe a career in underwriting can be so much more. You bring the passion and entrepreneurial spirit; we’ll provide the platform to unleash the very best of your talents and skills. Together, we’ll celebrate and reward success! Are you intrigued? Then read on and apply now to advance your career at Ledgebrook.

About the Role

We are seeking experienced Cyber Liability underwriting talent to join our growing team whose mission is focused on building a profitable book of cyber liability business. Our vision is to deliver market relevant solutions to our key wholesale trading partners in a more frictionless environment that places an emphasis on efficiencies and quality to meet or exceed our broker’s overall needs in a risk differentiated manner. If you possess an entrepreneurial passion that includes a proven track history of delivering underwriting excellence and are seeking an opportunity to break out of the traditional insurance company mould, we’re looking for you!

As a member of the Cyber team, you will regularly interact with our wholesale trading partners over the phone, virtually and in-person to drive submission flow and convert on the best opportunities quoted. We are looking for disciplined underwriting candidates that possess a strong overall cyber liability background with experience underwriting risks of all industries and sizes.

We are flexible with both a candidate’s experience level and physical work location. The actual position title (Underwriter, Senior UW, AVP, etc.) will be dependent on a candidate’s specific experience and qualifications. We currently operate in a fully remote work environment, so we’re more focused on your experience and cultural fit than where you physically sit!

About You

Here at Ledgebrook we’re passionate about creating a team that thrives on continuous learning and shares our excitement about building a company from the ground up. We’re looking for people to join us with:

●     A passion for delivering world-class customer service to our internal and external customers

●     Intellectual curiosity and a strong desire for innovation, rather than following the status quo

●     A hunger for continuous learning and opportunities to grow

●     Agile prioritization skills coupled with a keen sense of urgency - we balance getting it right with getting it done right now

●     A strong drive and desire to win together as a high-performing team

●     A moral compass to "do the right thing, period." We have zero tolerance for toxic behaviors

●     An eagerness to actively participate and connect with the whole team, across remote locations

●     An honest, transparent communication style

●     A proactive, solution-oriented mindset. We don’t look for blame, we look for the solution

As a future Cyber Liability Underwriter, your experience and qualifications must include:

●     2+ years experience as a cyber underwriter

●     Experience working in the Cyber E&S market; Tech E&O experience is a plus

●     Ability to work as a team player or independently in a fast-paced work environment

●     Deep wholesale broker trading relationships

●     Effective communication skills to articulate our appetite and develop wholesale broker relationships

●     Understanding of pricing and risk selection criteria to achieve underwriting profit

●     Advanced understanding of data analysis and execution of portfolio management objectives

●     Intellectual curiosity, problem solving skills, and a sense of urgency

●     Responsive, customer service focused mindset and behaviors

●     Ability to make timely decisions with appropriate information and consultation

●     A strong entrepreneurial drive and desire to build and win together as a high performing team

●     Ability to travel to meet with assigned brokers or with the broader team to participate in industry conference or events
